veredito_provisorio: ATTENTION, does not BLOCK (same outcome as R1, now extended to the 20 cells). The 2 km buffer is honored (node-to-node d_min ~2.000 km in all cells, test and val, against training). Between 3 and 5 of the 20 DECLARED test blocks per cell in g10b2 retain no node after the buffer (15-17 effective out of 20), always in EDGE blocks (last row/column of the grid, never interior) -- confirms and EXTENDS the R1 finding (Q1: 17/17/17/15) to the 12 cells Q2-Q4 that R1 left nao_verificado. In g5b2 (Bauru), 68 of 73 test blocks are effective, but 34-35 of those 68 are 'nearly empty' (retention <10% of the nodes the block had before the buffer) -- the finer 5 km grid is more sensitive to the same edge mechanism. VALIDATION blocks are much less affected: 19-20 of 20 effective in g10b2, 72/72 in g5b2. METHODOLOGICAL CAVEAT of this round: the reconstruction of the synthetic mesh (linspace over the lon/lat bounds of the run JSON) does NOT match the real ETL mesh bit for bit -- relative node-count error between 5e-6 and 2e-4 in all 20 cells (EXACT gate declared FAILED in 20/20; n_blocos per role matches exactly in 20/20). Where comparable (Q1 g10b2, 4 cities), the effective test blocks match EXACTLY the number already published in the internal note of 15/09 and confirmed with real npz in R1 (17/17/17/15) -- strong indication that the node-level error does not change the count of effective blocks in the cells already cross-checked, but this was NOT verified with real data in the remaining 16 cells of this round (Q2-Q4 g10b2, g5b2): treat as PROVISIONAL until an independent recalculation settles the origin of the relative error (candidate: float32 vs float64 precision between the original .pt and the synthetic mesh).
